mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher borrowing costs depressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar high-rate regimes, or FEDFUNDS drops below 5% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite consistent PAYEMS/UNRATE pattern in 5+ historical episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals robust economic demand for US goods.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns in 10 post-expansion INDPRO spikes across multiple sectors.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months suggests a cooling demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in 80% of CPIAUCSL < 3 periods across all economic states.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls by more than 0.25 percentage points from the prior quarter, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to turn positive as rate cuts are anticipated.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of FEDFUNDS falls > 0.25pp from prior quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite FEDFUNDS declines in all subsequent rate-cut events.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in housing starts (not available in the catalog; fallback: use HOUST as proxy for activity) combined with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market expansion signal predicting positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day returns when HOUST/UNRATE pattern repeats in contractionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% indicate a persistent supply-side easing, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in 60% of CPIAUCSL < 2 episodes across all data.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales proxy (not available; fallback: use PAYEMS as proxy for consumer demand) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) forms a demand strengthening signal predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in 5 historical demand expansion events.
